About

My research connects how people move through cities to questions of fairness, environment, and health. Across three strands, I study sustainable mobility and transport equity, multimodal transport system and adaptation, and environmental exposure and health inequalities, asking not only how cities move, but who gains and who is left behind.

I develop methods in spatial data science, machine learning, and GIS that turn anonymised individual mobile-phone trajectories and large-scale electronic health records into evidence at the level of individual people, streets, and neighbourhoods. This work has informed the UK Department for Transport, Transport for London, the Greater London Authority, Ordnance Survey, and the NHS, supporting sustainable transport policy, infrastructure resilience, and public health.

Research

develop data-driven approaches that combine geographic information science, urban analytics, network science, machine learning, and causal inference to understand how people move through cities and how these mobility patterns shape environmental exposures and health outcomes. Leveraging large-scale mobile-phone data and electronic health records, my research advances knowledge on transport equity, multimodal mobility, environmental exposure, and population health. This work is structured around three interconnected research themes. Click any theme to explore further.

Thread 01

Sustainable mobility and transport equity

Evaluating how transport interventions reshape mobility patterns within intervention areas and across the wider transport system and who benefits from these changes.
+

I combine mobile-phone GPS data with causal inference methods to evaluate transport and place-based interventions across multiple spatial scales. By examining impacts both within intervention areas and across the wider transport network, and by distinguishing between residents, visitors, and pass-through travellers, I reveal who benefits, who is disadvantaged, and how effects are distributed across populations and places.

Selected Project
  • Transport for London, Evaluating the mobility and distributional impacts of Low Traffic Neighbourhoods using individual-level mobility data.
  • Greater London Authority, Analysing group footfall dynamics and mobility patterns during major events and public-space interventions.
Featured work
Evaluating local-area transport interventions through mobile phone GPS data: a framework and case study of low traffic neighbourhoods (Transportation Research Part A, 2026)
A framework that pairs mobile-phone GPS data with causal inference to evaluate local-area interventions across travel modes and population groups, applied to a cluster of Low Traffic Neighbourhoods in north-east London.
Thread 02

Multimodal transport systems and adaptation

Reconstructing how entire cities move and adapt across transport modes, from everyday travel to major disruptions.
+

I develop artificial intelligence and GIS methods that transform anonymised mobile-phone trajectories into mode-specific, street-level flow estimates across walking, cycling, bus, rail, and car networks. By linking these flows into a city-wide mobility system, I study how people and transport networks respond to short- and long-term disruptions, informing applications in transport planning, resilience, routing, and decarbonisation

Selected Project
  • Ordnance Survey, Multimodal Routing Network enhancement
  • Transport for London, RoadLab 2 real-time driving and walking flows
  • Department for Transport, Travel behaviour adaptation during extreme weather
Featured work
Spatiotemporal dynamics of local transport greenhouse gases using mobile phone data (Journal of Transport Geography, 2026, open access)
A bottom-up framework that uses individual mobile-phone data to estimate and allocate urban transport greenhouse-gas emissions at high spatial and temporal resolution, tracing which traveller groups and places drive emissions to guide local decarbonisation.
Thread 03

Environmental exposure and health inequalities

Understanding how dynamic environmental exposures shape health and health inequalities across populations and places.
+

I develop dynamic measures of exposure to green space, blue space, air pollution, and the built environment by integrating mobility data and large-scale NHS electronic health records. My research examines how environmental and mobility-related exposures influence mental and physical health throughout daily life, generating evidence to support healthier, more equitable cities and communities.

Selected Project
  • GroundsWell, green and blue space for mental health
  • Data-HEART, North West environmental data asset
Featured work
Understanding How Green Space Accessibility and Utilisation Relate to Common Mental Health: A Cross-Sectional Study in North West England(Under Review)
Integrating mobile phone mobility data, environmental indicators, and NHS health records to reveal how green space accessibility and utilisation independently contribute to better mental health, with active engagement playing a particularly important role in nature-deprived communities.

Projects & grants

Principal investigator
Data-HEART (North West Household Environmental Asset for Regional Transformation)2026 to present
Principal Investigator · NHS North West Secure Data Environment, Data Accelerator Fund for Novel and Emerging Assets (DAFNEA) £36,353.76
Building a regional household-level environmental data asset for the North West within the NHS Secure Data Environment, linking environmental exposures to population and health data to enable research on environment, health inequality, and regional transformation.
Co-investigator
Multimodal Routing Network EnhancementOct 2024 to Dec 2025
Co-Investigator (PI: Prof. Tao Cheng) · Ordnance Survey £60,000
Integrating anonymised mobile-phone trajectories with the Ordnance Survey Multimodal Routing Network to infer mode-specific flows, and demonstrating how behavioural mobility data can enrich Great Britain's national transport-infrastructure datasets.
iMobility: Multi-Mode Mobility Monitoring and Analysis using Mobile GPS DataFeb 2024 to Feb 2025
Co-Investigator · Transport for London, RoadLab 2 Innovation Challenge £20,000
Generating near-real-time pedestrian and cyclist origin to destination flows and routes on Transport for London networks, validated against traffic counts and Vivacity cameras, to support cycling routing in the TfL Go app.
Researcher & contributor
GroundsWell: Community-engaged and Data-informed Systems Transformation of Urban Green and Blue Space for Population HealthFeb 2025 to present
Research Associate (Co-I: Prof. Mark Green) · UK Prevention Research Partnership
Developing dynamic metrics of access to and exposure to urban green and blue space, and conducting large-scale population-health analysis on NHS electronic health records via the CIPHA platform, linking environmental exposure to mental-health diagnoses and chronic-disease outcomes, and co-producing actionable insights with NHS partners and stakeholders such as The Mersey Forest.
Improving Flood-Disrupted Road Network Resilience with Dynamic People-Centric Digital TwinsMay 2024 to Feb 2025
Research Assistant (Co-I: Prof. Tao Cheng) · Data & Analytics Facility for National Infrastructures (DAFNI)
Developing hourly multimodal traffic-flow data across multi-layer London transport networks to power a people-centred digital-twin system, modelling cascading infrastructure vulnerability during urban flooding and linking flood-hazard modelling to dynamic population exposure and transport-system performance.
Understanding the Impact of COVID-19 and Non-Pharmaceutical Interventions on Mobility and Places in SingaporeNov 2023 to Feb 2025
Research Assistant (PI: Prof. Tao Cheng) · Alan Turing Institute
Adapting and testing the scalability of London-developed travel-mode detection for Singapore, designing the EcoTravel mobile app to collect labelled GPS training data, and building multi-year multimodal mobility datasets to evaluate travel behaviour, activity change, and the optimisation of non-pharmaceutical interventions.
Evaluating the Impacts of Low Traffic Neighbourhood Schemes on Transport System Operation and Travel BehaviourDec 2020 to Apr 2024
Research Assistant · Transport for London
Developing a machine-learning and GIS travel-mode detection algorithm classifying seven modes (car, bus, train, tube, cycle, walk, stationary) from mobile-phone data, producing London-wide multimodal mobility datasets from 2019 onward, and evaluating the short- and long-term effects of Low Traffic Neighbourhoods on the transport system and travel behaviour.
Travel-Behaviour Adaptation during Extreme-Weather EventsJun 2023 to Sep 2023
PhD Research Intern · Department for Transport (Advanced Analytics)
Independent analysis of how heatwaves and storm disruption reshape travel behaviour, accessibility, and system performance using large-scale national mobile-phone data, delivering evidence for national transport-resilience planning and comparing theoretical with actual transport connectivity.
Monitoring the Footfall of Multiple Groups and Their Responses to Special Events in LondonJun 2022 to Dec 2022
Research Assistant · Greater London Authority
Inferring home, workplace, and visited locations from mobile-phone data, generating and validating group-level hourly footfall datasets, and analysing footfall responses to events including tube strikes and the Queen's lying-in-state queue on the South Bank.
Multiscale Clustering Knowledge Mining and ApplicationsSep 2017 to Apr 2019
Research Assistant (PI: Prof. Yaolin Liu) · National Natural Science Foundation of China
Using remote-sensing and nighttime-light data to extract human activity, measuring types of urban land expansion, and analysing the spatiotemporal coupling of urban expansion, industrial structure, and regional integration across the Yangtze River Economic Belt.
